snapshot.readinessLevel: Moderate (67) — well rested overnight per Garmin (sleep 82%, recovery 92%, HRV 85% all GOOD), but multi-week sleep/stress history is still soft (~58%). Oura's own read this morning is more positive (readiness 78, "Good — ready to train").
snapshot.loadBalance: Aerobic-low focus (plenty of easy volume monthly; anaerobic and aerobic-high both trail behind it)

change: The gray zone is still the #1 lever: over the last 30 days only 42% of running time was genuinely easy (Z1-Z2, 39.0 mi) versus 47% sitting in Z3 (129-146 bpm, 44.5 mi) and 12% truly hard. The last 14 days are essentially flat (43% easy / 43% gray / 14% hard) — this hasn't improved yet, so keep watching HR on easy days and back off the moment it crosses ~130.

VO2max has been flat at 52-53 for two months (52.5 today) and training status reads "Maintaining" rather than "Productive." Monthly aerobic-low volume is healthy, but too much of the intended-easy running is drifting into Z3, which blunts the aerobic stimulus that would actually move VO2max.

Weekly mileage stepped back from 26.7 to 21.1 mi this week (partly a tennis night instead of a run, partly a lighter Saturday). Not a red flag — ACWR is still optimal at 0.8 — but it means there was no ramp this week, and there won't be one next week either.

The big news has nothing to do with the training data: the baby arrived today (Aug 9), earlier than the late-August due date. Next week's plan drops the ramp entirely — everything is optional, mileage is whatever happens organically, and the periodization clock resets to the newborn-maintenance phase a few weeks early.
continue: Quality days stay genuinely hard: Aug 4's threshold session put 42 of 62 minutes in Z4-Z5 combined, and Jul 28's VO2max intervals hit 22.6 of 53 minutes there. The intensity side of polarized training is real — it's the easy side that needs work.

Long-run execution keeps improving: Aug 1's 10-miler ran 54% of its time in Z1-Z2 and Jul 25's 9-miler ran 66% easy. Compare mid-July long runs that were mostly Z3 — same distances, better HR control.

ACWR has stayed optimal (0.8, acute 452 / chronic 546) through two weeks of up-and-down mileage — the body is absorbing the variability fine, which is a good sign heading into an unpredictable newborn stretch.
Sleep peaked right before it mattered most: Oura logged 7.7h at a 89 sleep score last night, the best of the week, right before a very different kind of sleep deprivation begins. Bank it.
